key_insight: Three multicriteria ranking methods identified hexagonal-pin welding at 1600 rpm, 15 mm/min and 0.3 mm plunge depth as the best strength–ductility compromise for polycarbonate–nylon-6 lap joints.
engineering_relevance: The results guide process and tool selection for joining dissimilar thermoplastic sheets when ductility matters alongside weld strength.
method: Varied rotational speed, traverse speed, plunge depth and tool pin profile in friction stir lap welding.
Used response surface methodology to model joint efficiency and weld hardness.
Combined AHP–entropy weights with CoCoSo, MABAC and grey relational analysis to rank welding conditions.
evidence_signal: All three methods selected a condition delivering 28.9 MPa strength and 17.1 mm elongation, with Spearman rank correlations of 0.951–0.991.
watch_item: The preferred condition reflects the chosen strength, elongation and hardness weights; ranking agreement alone does not establish robustness beyond the tested conditions.
paper_title: A Combined MCDM Approach for Parametric Hierarchy in Friction Stir Lap Welding of Dissimilar Polycarbonate to Nylon‐6
